sections.text:
```
+===========================================================================+
|                  SEA LEVEL — COMPONENTS AND CAUSES                        |
+===========================================================================+
|                                                                           |
|  EUSTATIC (global absolute sea level change)                              |
|  ─────────────────────────────────────────                                |
|  Ice volume change (glacio-eustasy)    ← dominant on glacial timescales  |
|  Thermal expansion of seawater         ← dominant on century timescales  |
|  Ocean basin volume change (tectonics) ← on >1 Myr timescales            |
|                                                                           |
|  ISOSTATIC (crustal deformation)                                          |
|  ─────────────────────────────────                                        |
|  Glacial isostatic adjustment (GIA): Earth rebounds after ice melts       |
|  Sediment loading / unloading                                             |
|  Tectonic uplift / subsidence                                             |
|                                                                           |
|  RELATIVE SEA LEVEL (RSL) = eustasy + local isostasy + local tectonics   |
|  (what matters for coastal flooding and planning)                         |
|                                                                           |
|  OCEAN DYNAMIC TOPOGRAPHY:                                                |
|  Sea surface height varies ±1–2 m geographically from geostrophic        |
|  currents, wind setup, gravity anomalies                                  |
+===========================================================================+
```

sections.text: Isostasy is Archimedes' principle applied to the crust: the lithosphere floats on the viscous asthenosphere at a depth proportional to its density, exactly as a ship floats at a waterline proportional to its loaded mass. GIA (Glacial Isostatic Adjustment) relaxation is a viscoelastic creep response: apply the load (ice sheet), the elastic lithosphere deflects instantly, then the viscous asthenosphere creeps slowly to equilibrium over thousands of years — mathematically a dashpot-spring (Kelvin-Voigt) model where the relaxation timescale τ = viscosity/elastic modulus of the mantle. Return-period (100-year flood, 500-year storm surge) is Extreme Value Theory (Gumbel, GEV distributions) — the same framework used in structural reliability engineering to size foundations, dams, and flood walls for a specified annual exceedance probability. With sea level rise the parent distribution is non-stationary — the return period of a fixed water level decreases as the mean shifts, requiring recalibration of all infrastructure design standards.
